sentence: Cake is wrong. The cake is wrong. The baker delivered a cake that is the wrong shape and the wrong color and the wrong filling and the cake is in the lobby and I have ninety minutes to get it fixed or replaced and the baker is not answering.

It is hitting the next subdivision. I can hear it. They say it sounds like a freight train and that is exactly what it sounds like and it is getting louder and the windows are rattling and my son is crying and I am holding him so tight he cannot breathe properly.

DJ is sick. Sick. He just texted. The DJ for my wedding tonight is sick. He cannot do it. He is sending a sub but the sub does not have my song list and the song list has my parents' first dance and the surprise song for the bridal party and the ceremony cues.

Bleeding. He cut his leg with the chainsaw. There is so much blood. So much. I am pressing a towel down and the towel is already soaked. Another towel. Another towel. The dispatcher says fifteen minutes for the ambulance and I am screaming that he does not have fifteen minutes.

911. He is not breathing. He is not breathing. I do not know how long. He was on the floor. I came in and he was on the floor. The dispatcher is asking me his age and I cannot remember if he is fifty-two or fifty-three. I cannot remember. Hurry. Please. Just send someone.

Ransom note on every workstation in the building. Bitcoin demand. Three days. Three days to pay or the encrypted data goes public and we cannot tell what is encrypted yet because half the backups also look encrypted now.

The baby. The baby is blue. I am doing the back blows. The video on the phone showed back blows. Between the shoulder blades. Hard. Harder than feels right. Five. Five back blows and then chest thrusts. My hands are too big for her body. I am too rough I am too rough I am going to break her.

Man overboard. Man overboard. I hit the MOB button and I have one hand on the wheel and I am circling back and the wake is white and I lost sight of him for two seconds and he is in a wetsuit and the swell is six feet.

Fight broke out in the next car. Glass shattered. People streaming through into our car and somebody is yelling for help and the train is in the tunnel between stops and the police will not get on until the next platform.

Toaster oven sparking on the counter. The cabinet above it is wood and it is going to go. I yanked the cord and the spark followed and now there is a small flame on the plastic housing and I am running to the sink for water but you do not use water on electrical, you do not, what do I do.
Six of us in here. Air feels thin. The lights cut to emergency mode and it is dim and the alarm bell is going and the cable just thunked overhead and we all looked up at the same time.

Phishing email got through the filter and the controller clicked it and now somebody has the controller's credentials and there were six wire transfers initiated overnight totaling four hundred thousand dollars and the wires already went out.

Smoke in the cabin. Real smoke. People are coughing and the lights have gone to dim emergency and the captain is asking flight attendants to prepare for emergency landing and we are over water and I cannot tell where the nearest airport is.

Bloomberg just flashed that the bank failed. The bank. Our exposure to that bank is everything. Everything. I have to call the head of risk in the next sixty seconds and I do not know what the number is, I do not know how big our position is, I am pulling up the report and the report will not load.

Power went out during the trade. The order was halfway through and the screen went black and when the backup booted thirty seconds later the position had moved against me by eleven percent and I do not know if the order filled or got cancelled.

Running through the lobby. The information desk is asking my name. I am asking for the trauma wing. They are asking me to spell my name. SPELL MY NAME. I am spelling my name. Where is my mother. Where is she.

Leash slipped. Slipped right out of my hand. He is running into the street and there is a car coming and I am sprinting and calling his name and he cannot hear me over the traffic and the driver is not slowing.

Boarding announcement just went. Final call. I am in the security line and my belt is in the tray and the laptop is on the conveyor and there are six people ahead of me and the gate is at the far end of the airport.
Eclampsia. Patient just started seizing. Magnesium. Two milligrams of Ativan. Roll her. Roll her on her side. Where is the husband. Get the husband out. Get him out of the room he is going to faint.
Doors closed on my bag. My bag is half in the train and half on the platform and the train started to move and I have one hand on the strap and one hand on the pole and the strap is fraying.

The car in front slammed on the brakes and I rear ended them and the car behind me rear ended me and we are all on the freeway in three lanes of seventy mile an hour traffic. Get out. Hazards on. Get to the shoulder. Run. Cars are still coming. They are not slowing down. They are not slowing down.

Aftershock. Another one. Smaller but the building was already weakened and I can hear something giving way and a beam dropped in the next room and dust is coming through the crack in the door and we cannot stay here.

Wrong audio. The clip that just played was a different story than the one I introduced and the listeners are going to be confused and the program director is on line two and I have one minute to fix this before the next segment.

Black ice. The back end is sliding. I am steering into it and it is not catching. The guardrail is coming up fast. Brake brake brake. Do not brake. Which one. Which one. I cannot remember. Impact. Airbag. The world goes white and then there is the smell of burning plastic and I am upside down.

Bus broke down in the middle of nowhere. The driver is on the side of the road on his phone and the next show is in seven hours in another state and the equipment is in the trailer and the trailer is hitched to a bus that will not start.

Mom won't leave. She won't leave the house. The storm surge is supposed to be twelve feet and her front door is six feet above sea level and I am on the phone begging her and she is telling me she has been through worse and there is no worse than this, there is no worse than this.

Hard candy. He had a hard candy in his pocket I did not know about. He just came up to me with his mouth open and pointing at his throat and not making any sound and I have him over my knee and pounding.

Hit and run. The car that hit me just drove off. I am bleeding from a cut on my head and the back of my car is folded and I am trying to read the license plate from memory and I only got three digits.

Coffee just spilled on my shirt. The whole front of the shirt. The interview is at the cafe in nine minutes. The cafe is two blocks. The shirt is light blue and the stain is enormous. I have no other shirt. I have to walk into this interview looking like I attacked a vending machine.

Verdict came in. The jury is coming back. We had a deadlocked Allen charge an hour ago and now they are coming back and my client is asking what does this mean and I do not know what it means and the bailiff is opening the door.

Figure 3 will not render. The vector file just becomes a black square in the PDF. I am redoing it from scratch in twenty minutes. Twenty minutes. The original took me two days. Exporting again. The export is hanging. Why does Illustrator hate me right now of all moments.

Twelve minutes. The submission portal closes at midnight and the final section is still two paragraphs short. My hands are shaking on the keyboard. Save, save, save. Why does the cursor keep skipping. I keep retyping the same sentence and it sounds worse each time. Eleven minutes now. There is no time to re-read. There is no time to think. Just words, any words, into the box and click submit before the clock turns over.

Mistrial. Opposing counsel is moving for a mistrial because my witness mentioned the insurance policy and you cannot mention the insurance policy and the judge is calling us up to the bench and I have to come up with a reason why this is not a mistrial in the next thirty seconds.

Glass breaking downstairs. Just shattered. I am sitting up in bed and the dog is growling and the front-door alarm did not go off and someone is in the house. Someone is in the house. Where is the phone. WHERE IS THE PHONE.

Wrong link. I clicked the wrong link. The Zoom is showing me an empty meeting and the meeting I am supposed to be in is the OTHER one and my hands are sweating and I am refreshing my inbox and the recruiter texted six minutes ago asking where I am.

Airway. Airway is closed. He is gasping and his lips are blue and I am cricking the head back and the jaw is rigid and I am reaching for the NPA and the NPA is in my other bag and the other bag is across the road.

GPS just rerouted us through downtown and we are sitting at a red light watching the minutes tick over and my sister is supposed to walk down the aisle in nineteen minutes and we are still six miles away. The driver is honking. Everyone is honking. Nothing is moving. I am the maid of honor. I have the rings.

Backup is corrupted. The off-site backup is corrupted. The on-site backups are encrypted by the ransomware. The cold storage tapes are three months old. THREE months. We are about to lose three months of customer activity if we cannot decrypt and the FBI is telling us not to pay.

The motorcycle is down. The motorcycle is down ten feet from my hood. I did not see him. He came out of the blind spot. I am running across the intersection with my hands shaking and people are honking at me and I am yelling do not move do not move and he is not moving anyway.

Eighty-six the scallops. Eighty-six the scallops. We are out and the floor still has the dish on the menu and the table just ordered three and the manager is at the pass and the supplier cannot deliver until tomorrow.

He is asking if he is going to make it. I cannot tell him. I cannot tell him yes or no and his hand is gripping mine and I am pretending to look at his bandage to avoid his eyes and the medevac is inbound and the LZ is not secure.

Six months. He is six months old and he choked on a piece of cracker the older one gave him and I have him face down on my forearm with his head lower than his body and I am hitting between the shoulder blades and his lips are gray.

Pregnant. I am pregnant and stuck in an elevator and the contractions are starting and the emergency line is on hold and the music is playing and I am breathing through my nose and counting and the next one is coming faster than the last.

Heard a pop. A pop and then two more and then I heard people running and the door at the end of the hallway slammed and I am huddled under a desk in the conference room and I cannot remember if I locked the door behind me.

She was right here. She was holding the edge of the cart. I turned for two seconds. The cereal aisle is empty. I am calling her name. Other shoppers are turning. Maya. Maya. The fluorescent lights are too bright. My voice is getting higher. I do not recognize my own voice. Where is she. Where is she.

IV will not start. Veins are flat. He is bled out enough that the veins collapsed and I have a peripheral kit and the IO drill in my pack and I am drilling the humerus and the patient is unconscious and the next round is coming in over the wall.

Dog is going crazy at the back door. Going CRAZY. Barking and growling and lunging and someone is on the deck and I can see a shape through the curtain and the curtain is moving like they are trying the lock.

Truck rolled out without the chock. The driver is back at the cab and not paying attention and the truck is rolling slowly toward the open dock and there is no one between to stop it and the dock is fifteen feet to a drop.
Cell tower is down. The router is dead. Internet is gone. The phone is showing zero bars and I am supposed to be on a conference call in eight minutes with a client and there is no way to reach them.

Boat capsized. Three kids in the water without life jackets. The current is moving them downstream and one of them cannot swim and I am running along the bank trying to get ahead of them so I can throw the rope.

Caller line is dead. The phone system crashed. I am supposed to do twenty minutes of talkback right now and there are no calls and the producer is across the hall trying to reboot the phone system and the dead air is filling and I am alone with a microphone.

Bird strike. Both engines surged at takeoff and the plane is climbing slow and the captain is on the radio with the tower and the wings are level but the airspeed is bleeding and we cleared the runway by twenty feet.

Toddler at the pool gate. Pool gate left open. I just saw her toddle toward the water and I am running and she is one step from the edge and I am not going to get there, I am not going to get there in time.

Hospital. Hospital lockdown. Code silver, code silver overhead, and I am in the middle of placing a chest tube and the nurse just bolted the door and the patient is awake and asking me what is happening and I have to keep working because I cannot stop now.

Conveyor jammed and the belt is still trying to drive. The motor is whining and smoking and the operator's hand is caught in the rollers and I am hitting the emergency stop and the e-stop is not stopping it.

I see him. I see him at the end of the alley. Do not run. Do not run, walk slowly, treats out. Treats out. He is watching me. He is going to bolt. He is going to bolt the moment I get within ten feet. Slower. Slower.

Patient is seizing. Tonic-clonic, full body. Roll him. Roll him on his side. Ativan, ativan, where is the ativan. Two milligrams IV push. He just bit his tongue. There is blood. There is so much blood and his eyes are rolled back.

Front door is hot. Do not open it. Do not open it. Back door. Back door. Climbing over the couch. The smoke is settling lower than my head now. I am holding a wet dish towel to my mouth. I have always read that you do that. I never thought I would do that. The latch is sticking. Why is the latch sticking.

Office. Phone notification said active threat on campus. We are in the supply closet, five of us, the closet, the door does not lock and I am holding the handle and bracing my legs against the wall and one of my coworkers is praying out loud and asking us to pray with her.

Hemorrhaging. The drain is filling. Liter, liter and a half in twenty minutes. Get type and cross to send STAT. Get the mass transfusion protocol started. Call surgery. The surgeon needs to be back in here in the next ten minutes or we lose this patient.

Wave knocked her down and the next wave is coming and she has not stood back up. The water is white and frothing and her dad is sprinting from the chair and the lifeguard is blowing the whistle and the next set is breaking and I cannot see her.

Down twelve percent at the open. Twelve. I am watching my retirement evaporate in real time and the broker's website keeps timing out every time I try to log in and I cannot even place a sell order because the order book is moving faster than the screen can refresh.

Cancelled. The driver just cancelled four minutes after pickup and pulled over and asked me to get out and there is no other car for sixteen minutes and I am on a corner I do not recognize with my luggage.

Database connections at 100%. Can't get a read. Can't get a write. The dashboard is solid red across every region. Slack notifications stacking up faster than I can dismiss them. Engineering VP just joined the call. Where is the runbook. Where IS the runbook. I had it open ten minutes ago.

Embers. Embers in the gutters. The roof is dry shake. I am on the ladder with the hose and the wind is blowing the embers under the eaves and I cannot get to them and the neighbor's pine just caught and the flames are jumping.

Confirmed touchdown. The TV anchor just said confirmed touchdown and he sounds scared and the radar shows the hook echo and the hook echo is over our county and I have to call my mother and tell her to get to the cellar but the call will not connect.

Phone alert just buzzed. Tornado on the ground three miles southwest, moving northeast at forty miles per hour. We are northeast. We are NORTHEAST. That gives us four minutes. Maybe four minutes. Get into the bathtub. Pull the mattress over us. Now. Now.

Bee sting. Bee sting to the neck and he is going into shock. Sitting on the trail, ten miles from the trailhead. No service. No epipen. No service. Pulse is fast and thready and we are trying to get a signal out and the bars keep flickering.

Second tourniquet. Need a second tourniquet. The first one is on the thigh and the bleeding shifted to the calf and I am out of tourniquets. I am out. I am using a belt and torquing it with a pen and watching the bleeding slow.

Brace for impact. The captain just said brace for impact. Brace for impact. I am bent forward with my head on the seat in front of me and the flight attendants are shouting commands and I do not know what we hit or what is happening or where we are.

Oil caught. Oil just caught in the pan and the flames are licking up to the cabinet and I am reaching for water, no, NOT water, what do I do, baking soda, salt, lid, LID, get the lid on it, where is the lid.

It is on top of us. The lights just went out. The pressure changed. My ears popped. Crouching. Crouching down. Something just hit the side of the house. Something big. The dog is screaming. I have never heard a dog make this sound.
Road is closed. The road out is closed. The other way is closed too. We are turning around in the driveway and there is no third option and the air is thick with smoke and the kids are coughing.
Lost a glove. Lost a glove in the slide. Lost a ski. The temperature is dropping and I am sitting in a hole I made and trying to call out and my phone is wet and the screen is blank.

Got out. Driving through ash and burning leaves and the dashboard says one-oh-eight outside and there is fire on both sides of the road and the kids are in the back covering their faces and the next exit is six miles.

Bed seven, bed seven, asystole. CPR started. Get the cart. Get the cart NOW. Where is anesthesia. Page anesthesia again. Compressions. Switch. Switch. Two milligrams of epi in. Charge the paddles. Clear. Clear, clear. Nothing. Resume.

Highway shoulder. I am standing on the highway shoulder waving at oncoming cars and the wrecked car is in the middle lane and the driver is unconscious and the next car is going to hit it if I cannot get them to slow.

The limo broke down. On the highway. With the bride in it. In her dress. The driver is looking under the hood and shaking his head and the bride is crying and the wedding planner is on the phone screaming and I do not know how we get her to the venue in fifteen minutes.

Guest is meltdown. The guest is screaming at the other guest and they are both standing and the moderator is trying to interrupt and the camera is wide and the network is going to see this and there is no commercial coming up for nine minutes.

Baby's heart rate is dropping. Dropping. Sixty. Fifty-five. We need to deliver this baby NOW. Get the OR ready. Page the on-call OB. The mother is asking what is happening and I do not have time to answer her and the nurse is wheeling the bed and the wheels are catching on the threshold.

Frozen pipe just thawed and burst behind the wall. Behind the wall. I cannot get to it. Water is running down inside the drywall and pooling at the baseboard and I am calling the emergency plumber and they say two hours minimum and the drywall is going to come down.

Lifejacket is not inflating. The CO2 cartridge must be empty. I am pulling the manual tube and blowing into it and my lungs are full of saltwater and there is a wave coming and I am not strong enough to fight it.

I am late. I am so late. The driver is following the route but the route is in massive traffic and the meeting starts in seven minutes and the destination is still nineteen minutes away and I am watching the ETA tick up not down.

Smoke. There is smoke in the car. Smoke coming from the back of the train and people are pushing toward the front and the door between cars is jammed and someone is pulling at it and the smoke is getting heavier.

Bridesmaid did not show up. Has not answered her phone since last night. The procession is supposed to be even and now we are uneven and people are showing up and the photographer wants to do the group shots and we have an empty space where she should be.
Backpack on the platform. Unattended. The whole subway station is being cleared and we are pouring up the stairs and someone is pushing and someone fell and the crowd is not stopping for them.

Eleven-fifty-seven on April fifteenth. Three minutes. The e-file is uploading and the progress bar is at sixty-three percent and I do not know if it will finish in time and I am refreshing the tracker and the spinner just keeps spinning.

Word count over by four hundred. Submission portal hard-rejects anything over the limit. I am cutting paragraphs at random because I cannot read carefully enough to choose and the clock is ticking and my advisor will not pick up the phone.
Mandatory evacuation order just came through the radio. Mandatory. They are not waiting. The bridge closes at six. The bridge is the only way out. It is four-thirty. We have not packed.
Smoke alarm screaming. The whole apartment is fogging up. Get the dog out. Get the dog out. The hallway is filling. The door, the door, my hand on the door, is it hot, it is not hot, open it, GO.

Restaurant. Public restaurant and my daughter is choking and everyone is staring and the waiter is calling 911 and I have her over my arm and pounding her back and the family at the next table is asking what they can do.

Passport expires in two months. The destination requires six months validity. I just learned this at the check-in counter and the flight leaves in two hours and they will not let me board and the next flight is in two days.

Chest pain. Left arm. He is grey. He is grey. I am dialing with one hand and unlocking the front door with the other so the paramedics can get in fast. Aspirin. The bottle is in the bathroom. I am sprinting up the stairs and the dispatcher is asking me questions and I am not answering, I am running.
Officiant just texted that he is stuck in traffic on the bridge. The ceremony starts in twelve minutes. Who else can do this. Who in this room is ordained. Anyone. Anyone.

Down twenty-two percent. Just kept selling. Just kept selling and now I am sitting here looking at a P&L that does not seem real and my hands are cold and I think I am going to be sick and there is still an hour left in the trading day.

Baby is not crying. Just came out and the baby is not crying. Suction. Dry. Stimulate. Toes blue. Apgar is one. Bag her. Bag her now. The nurse just hit the code button and the NICU team is running down the hall.

Pencils down in thirty seconds. Thirty. I have one essay left and a conclusion to write and I am writing as fast as my hand will let me and the words are coming out as scribbles and I cannot even read my own handwriting back.

I left the calculator in the car. The car is in the garage three blocks away. The proctor said no leaving and re-entering. The first problem is a derivative I can do in my head but problem two needs the calculator and I am already behind and oh god oh god think think think.

Train delayed forty minutes. Forty minutes. The onsite was at ten and it is twenty after and I am pacing the platform and the announcement keeps saying we apologize for the inconvenience and I am calling the recruiter and she is not picking up and the dot dot dot on my email is not going through.

Highway overpass. The car is rocking. The highway is rocking. The pillars holding up the overpass are visibly moving. Get off, get off, get off the road, but you are not supposed to be on the road and not supposed to be near a building, where ARE you supposed to be.

Dress has a stain. Right down the front of the bodice. Foundation. I just put on makeup and brushed the dress and now the dress has makeup on it and the photographer is here in thirty minutes and the seamstress is two hours away.

Co-counsel just lateralled out of the firm. This morning. THIS MORNING. The trial starts in three hours and she had the entire damages portion and now I have to handle it and I have not opened those binders since the prep meeting six weeks ago.

He is not answering. He always answers. I am calling his name in the voice he listens to and he is not answering. The mall is full of music and laughing kids and none of them are mine. I am turning in a slow circle in the middle of the food court and the world is tilting.

Grid is down. Utility just announced rolling blackouts but ours has been off for two hours and the heat is dropping and the pipes will freeze if it gets below twenty and the next rotation is in fifteen minutes.

The grant cycle ends at five and my advisor still has not signed the cover sheet. I am sprinting across the quad. My laptop bag is hitting my back with every step. If she is not in her office I do not know what I will do. Four-fifty. The building door is heavier than I remember. Stairs, take the stairs, the elevator is too slow.

Venue cancelled. They just emailed. Twelve hours before doors. Some permit issue. Fifteen hundred tickets sold. The promoter is on the phone screaming at me and the merch truck is already at the loading dock and I do not know what to do with everyone.

Hot mic. My co-host's mic is hot during the song and she is talking about a sponsor in extremely unflattering terms and the song is over in twelve seconds and I cannot get to her in time and the levels are showing her voice clearly.
Power is out. Pump is electric. The well pump is electric and the hose is empty and there is nothing to wet the roof with and the fire is two ridges over and the wind is at our backs.

Curtain caught from the candle. The whole curtain is going up and the flames are climbing toward the ceiling and the smoke detector finally went off and the kids are in the back room and I am screaming their names and they are not answering.

Hit and run. He hit me and kept going. License plate. License plate. I am trying to read it as he disappears. I am repeating it out loud. Three letters then four numbers. Four numbers. Repeat repeat repeat until I can type it. Do not lose it. Do not lose it.

The Scantron. I bubbled the wrong row. I bubbled the wrong row for the last fifteen questions. Erasing. Erasing faster. The eraser is smearing and tearing little flakes into the bubbles and I cannot get them clean and the timer is going and my hands won't stop shaking.

Microphone is not working. They can see me, they cannot hear me. I am clicking through settings and unplugging the headphones and plugging them back in and the interviewer is asking me to type in the chat and I cannot find the chat and my screen is frozen.

Coughing. He was coughing and now he is silent. Silent is worse than coughing. The hot dog. I told them no hot dogs uncut. Babies cannot have whole hot dogs. Heimlich. Heimlich. The baby version. The baby is too small for the adult version what is the baby version.

Pyrotechnic failure. The blast was supposed to be downstage right at the climax and it is going off NOW upstage left and the stage manager is screaming in my earpiece and I have to get the cast off that part of the stage in three counts.
Capsized. We rolled. The boat rolled in the swell and we are in the water and the boat is upside down and the dinghy is somewhere and I am counting heads. One. Two. Three. WHERE IS THE FOURTH.

Groom is having a meltdown. Locked himself in the bathroom and is not answering and the best man is talking to him through the door and the ceremony is in two hours and the cars are arriving and the bride's mother is asking what is happening.

Window in the basement broke. The alarm panel is showing zone 6 tripped and I am pulling up the camera and the camera is offline and the police are eighteen minutes out and the only thing between us is a thin pocket door.

Alarm just went off and the announcement is saying evacuate, evacuate, all personnel evacuate immediately and people are flooding the stairwells and someone is screaming about the third floor and I cannot find my badge and the security guard is at the door waving everyone out.

Boarding pass is for a different city. Different CITY. The agent printed it wrong and I just saw it at the gate and the plane to the right city is leaving from the next concourse and the doors close in nine minutes.
Highway. He is heading toward the highway. I can see him at the end of the access road and the cars are doing seventy and I am running and waving and the drivers cannot tell what I want them to do.

ICU. The ICU power just blipped. Backup generator kicked in but one of the vents took thirty seconds to come back online and the patient is on bypass and I can see the monitor recovering and I am holding my breath and watching the numbers come back.

Police are outside. Bullhorn telling us to come out with our hands up. Are they really police. Could the shooter say he is police. The kids are asking what to do and I am the teacher and I am supposed to know and I do not know.

Opposing counsel just introduced an exhibit I have never seen before. Never seen. They are claiming it was disclosed in discovery and I cannot remember and my client is sweating next to me and the judge is asking if I have any objection and I need to object but I do not have the grounds prepared.

Pallet is falling. Pallet is falling off the top rack and there is a worker below and I am screaming and waving and the worker is wearing earbuds and not turning and the pallet is tipping and going to come down right on him.

The truck did not stop. The truck did not stop. I am pulling onto the shoulder and my hands will not let go of the wheel. Get out. Get out and check. The other driver is moving. He is moving. Someone is screaming. I think the screaming is me. Glass everywhere. Glass in my lap. My phone is in the footwell and I cannot reach it.

Truck jackknifed in front of us. Brakes locked. Tires screaming. Hit it. Hit the side of the trailer at forty miles an hour and the airbags went off and the dust is white in the cabin and I cannot tell if my kid in the back seat is okay.

Dishwasher exploded. The hose blew off the back and the dishwasher is still pumping water out across the kitchen floor and I cannot get to the cutoff without going through the puddle and the puddle is reaching the outlet for the refrigerator.

Apartment building. Twelve floors. The elevator stopped between floors and there is a man stuck in there with chest pains and I am running down twelve flights of stairs in the dark to find a phone that works because the building intercom is also dead.

Breaking news mid-segment. Producer in my ear saying go go go to the story I have not read yet. The package is loading on the screen and I have one line on a piece of paper and I am supposed to talk for forty seconds and I do not even know who the people in the story are.

EAS tone. The Emergency Alert System tone just fired and I did not initiate it and I have no idea what alert it is. The screen is blank. The script printer is jammed. I have to read something on air and I do not have the something to read.

Door slipped open. Just slipped, the wind caught it, and the dog bolted. I am running barefoot down the sidewalk in pajamas and he is two blocks ahead and pulling further and I cannot see him at the next corner.

I am alone in here. Alone. The doors closed on the parking garage level and the elevator dropped and the brake caught and now it is just hanging and I am pounding on the door and there is nobody in the garage at this hour.

Apartment below me is calling. They have water coming through their ceiling. I am running through every room and the kitchen sink cabinet is dripping out the bottom and there is a steady spray under the sink and the disposal is still running and I am yanking everything open.

Smelling smoke. There is smoke coming from somewhere and the elevator is stuck and the smoke is curling in through the gap at the top of the door and I am breathing through my sleeve and pressing the lobby button over and over.

Two children. Both eating dinner. I turned around to get a napkin and when I turned back the younger one was blue and the older one was running for me and the younger one was on the floor and not making any noise.

Lead singer is sick. Like really sick. Cannot speak. Cannot speak and the show is in three hours and twelve hundred people have tickets and we cannot refund and we cannot reschedule and the opener is already in the venue.

Boarding in fifteen minutes. The kiosk just spat out the passport and the bag tag will not print. The bag has a check-in deadline of twelve minutes from now and the line for the agent is forty deep and I am the only one who can resolve this.

Gate latch broken. Has been broken for who knows how long. The dog has been gone since this morning and we just got home and the gate was open and his bed is empty and there is no sign in the yard and dusk is coming fast.

Eight people. Capacity is supposed to be eight. We are eight. We were eight when it stopped. Now everyone is breathing the same air and one guy is sweating through his shirt and somebody is pressing the call button repeatedly and the operator just said three minutes which she said twelve minutes ago.

Margin call. Margin call email just came through. They want forty-seven thousand dollars by end of day or they liquidate the entire position at whatever it trades for. The market is down nine percent. The position is down twenty. I do not have forty-seven thousand dollars in cash.

I just used the wrong client name in opening statement. The whole opening. I have been calling her by the previous case's plaintiff. The judge made a face. The jury looks confused. I have to call her by her real name from here on and pretend that did not happen.

Shoulder dystocia. The head delivered and the shoulder is stuck. McRoberts. Suprapubic pressure. Rotate. Rotate. The clock is running. We have about six minutes before the brain damage and we are already at four.
